source.label: Margot, Gladman & Yang (2024), PSJ, doi:10.3847/PSJ/ad55f3, equations 3–5

limitations: The IAU 2006 resolution supplies a qualitative definition; this numeric clearing threshold is a research model, not an official IAU numeric test.
The adopted published shortcut assumes a solar-mass host, a 10-billion-year clearing time and C=2 sqrt(3) Hill radii. This is not the current age of the Solar System.

The expression is an idealized circular-orbit diffusive clearing model. Evaluating it at the semimajor axis of an eccentric orbit is a reference calculation, not a validated eccentric-orbit clearance requirement.
Other planets, resonances, dynamical friction, gas drag, disk tides, migration and full N-body history are not solved.
A clearing ability under a specified time horizon is not an observation that all neighbouring bodies are absent. Satellites, Trojan populations and orbit-crossing minor bodies can remain.

The coefficient 0.001239 is adopted as published. Pi is calculated by direct division; the separately rounded published 807 coefficient is metadata only. Rounded general-form constants need not reproduce this shortcut to machine precision.
Pi is dimensionless, not an existence probability, confidence percentage, measured clearing fraction or independent reclassification.

summary.range_definition: Envelope of six named source moon bulk densities +/- their reported sigma and each adopted target radius's quoted offsets, used only as arithmetic parameter corners; missing radius uncertainty is held at the nominal radius. Not a joint confidence interval, physical density bound, likelihood or exhaustive census.

limitations: Every computed mass is a conditional radius/density hypothesis, not a separately measured primary mass; the original mass, IAU criteria and official classification are unchanged.
Similar size or an icy surface does not establish equal bulk density: rock/ice composition, internal porosity, thermal history and gravitational compression can differ.
The six moons are named, size-comparable examples, not a statistically representative population, a calibrated density prior, or an exhaustive search of possible densities.
A spherical volume is assumed. Thermal-model size, projected occultation area, a rendered sphere and hydrostatic equilibrium are different concepts.
Source plus/minus offsets used as parameter endpoints do not become a confidence interval for this different body's mass; no joint covariance or probability is computed.
The density input interval 100 to 10000 kg/m^3 is an interface/model operating range, not a universal physical bound or a measured density interval for any target.
The optional Margot comparison remains the fixed circular solar 10 Gyr reference at the source semimajor axis; especially for Sedna it is not a validated eccentric-orbit clearing requirement.
Meeting a conditional numeric clearing model alone neither establishes hydrostatic equilibrium nor changes an IAU classification or supplies a planet-existence probability.
source_selection_policy: New analogue inputs use NASA/JPL and qualitative NASA NTRS references; previously adopted radius facts retain their observatory/provider and publication-host identity. No new Chinese-agency data or archive is adopted; author nationality is not inferred or filtered.
rights: Project-authored factual snapshots and calculations; full upstream publications are local audit only.
